definition: Telephone theory is a historical theory of hearing, associated here with Rutherford, holding that the organ of Corti vibrates as a single unit and sends the auditory nerve a matching number of impulses for each movement of the eardrum and stapes. On this view, the brain’s auditory centres perform the analysis of these signals.
